name: Dhamma Pubbananda
tradition: Vipassana Meditation as taught by S.N. Goenka (Sayagyi U Ba Khin tradition)
technique: Anapana (breath awareness) and Vipassana (systematic body-scanning meditation), taught via S.N. Goenka's recorded audio and video instructions.
teacherAccess: Certified assistant teachers guide students through Goenka's recorded instructions, with a few in-person meetings and limited time for questions during the course.
retreatOptions: Mainly standard 10-day residential courses, plus 1-3 day short courses, occasional 20-day old-student courses, and separate children's (8-12) and teens' (13-17) Anapana courses.
about: Dhamma Pubbananda, meaning "Joy of the East," is a Vipassana meditation center on 13 acres in a quiet residential neighborhood of Claymont, Delaware, and is notable as the first urban Vipassana center in North America. The property was purchased in 2013 by the Mid-Atlantic Vipassana Association and opened its first building in 2014, with current capacity for 60 students and 14 servers across roughly 20 ten-day courses a year, alongside old-student and youth programs. As with all centers in the Goenka tradition, it is an all-volunteer, donor-funded 501(c)(3) nonprofit that teaches the technique free of charge through Goenka's recorded instructions and evening video discourses. Accommodations are a mix of shared dormitory rooms and a growing number of single rooms with en suite bathrooms as the center's masterplan is completed in phases. Students observe Noble Silence through the ninth of the ten days while following a structured meditation schedule and eating a simple vegetarian menu prepared by volunteer servers. Its central Mid-Atlantic location gives it easy access by car, train, and bus from Philadelphia, Baltimore, Washington DC, and New York.
schedule: Daily schedule runs roughly 4:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. with about 10 hours of meditation and an evening video discourse by S.N. Goenka; Noble Silence is kept through day nine of the ten-day course.
cost: No charge for teaching, food, or lodging; courses run strictly on voluntary dana from students who have completed at least one prior course, given only after finishing a course.

pricePerDay.notes: Strictly donation-based with no suggested amount; first-time students may give a donation only at the end of the course, based on their own means, and donations are accepted only from those who have already completed a course.

foodNotes: A simple vegetarian menu is provided to all students; no outside food or special requests are accommodated except for documented medical conditions.
workNotes: Course students are not required to work; the center is staffed by separate volunteer "servers," though old students may separately apply for dedicated service periods.
